Usage: curb <namespace|command> [options]

   curb — a C# formatter driven by your .editorconfig

Global options:
  -h, --help  Show help.
  --version   Show version.

Commands:
  check         Exit non-zero if anything would change.
  cleanup       Apply the code style fixes a build already reported.
  doc-tree      Dump the document IR for a file.
  format        Format files in place.
  options       Show which .editorconfig keys Curb implements.
  print-config  Show the resolved options and any diagnostics for a file.
  rules         Show which code style rules Curb fixes, and which it does not.

result.stdout:
Usage: curb check [<path>] [options]

   Exit non-zero if anything would change.

Arguments:
  [<path>]  A file or directory to check. [default: .]

Global options:
  -h, --help                      Show help.

Options:
  -f, --files <values>            [repeatable] Check only these, instead of walking path. May be given more than once. [default: null]
  --msbuild-list-file <file>      What the MSBuild integration passes instead of files: a file listing one path
per line, since a project's compile set can be too long for a command line to hold directly. [default: null] [existing]
  -c, --cache <string>            Skip files a previous run watched format to themselves. [default: null]
  --no-verify                     Skip re-parsing output to prove the token stream is unchanged.
  --expand-unhandled              Benchmark-only cost model: pretend every syntax kind has a dedicated printer.
  --coverage                      Report which syntax kinds are still emitted verbatim.
  --unformatted-list-file <file>  Write the paths that would change to this file, one per line. What the MSBuild integration reads
back to attach CURB0001 to each unformatted file instead of to the project. [default: null]

result.stdout:
Usage: curb cleanup [<path>] [options]

   Apply the code style fixes a build already reported.

Arguments:
  [<path>]  Where to look for curb.sarif logs, and which files to clean. [default: .]

Global options:
  -h, --help                  Show help.

Options:
  -s, --sarif-log <values>    [repeatable] The log to read, instead of searching path for
curb.sarif. May be given more than once, so a solution's per-project logs can all be
handed over in one run. [default: null]
  -f, --files <values>        [repeatable] Restrict cleanup to these, instead of every file the logs mention. May be given more than once. [default: null]
  --msbuild-list-file <file>  What the MSBuild integration passes instead of files: a file listing one path
per line, since a project's compile set can be too long for a command line to hold directly. [default: null] [existing]
  --check                     Report what would be fixed, change nothing.
  --forward                   Hand what Curb cannot fix to dotnet format, scoped to the reported rules and files, and
report both timings.
  --no-whitespace             With forward, run dotnet format style and dotnet format analyzers
as two separate invocations instead of one bare dotnet format. The default runs whitespace
too, which is a no-op against Curb's own output, in exchange for loading the MSBuild workspace once
instead of twice.

Notes:  Cleanup never builds. Build first, then run it: dotnet build && curb cleanup.
